plan_a_advantages: Reduced risk of overtraining due to the high volume of easy runs.
Potentially better for a runner who is currently fatigued or needs significant recovery.
plan_b_advantages: Directly targets speed development with the tempo run.
Includes longer runs that build trail-specific endurance and leg strength.
Introduces a structured effort beyond just easy running, promoting physiological adaptation.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on easy runs, which is beneficial for recovery, it lacks any structured efforts to improve speed or running economy. Plan B incorporates a tempo run and two longer runs at an easy pace, directly addressing the goal of increasing speed and building endurance – crucial components for trail running performance. The inclusion of a dedicated tempo session is a key differentiator that Plan A completely misses.
